solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Showing impertinence precludes fist flying

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters of the two words scattering through the air and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: Insolent behaviour shows itself when someone throws a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' signals an anagram of all thirteen letters of PRECLUDES and FIST together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rude and lacking deference to others is exactly a show of impertinence, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Be unable to stand, half-dead before trial

indicators.note: half asks for just the front two letters of the four-letter word dead

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Someone half-dead and facing trial can hardly stay on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-dead' looks like a description of an exhausted person, but 'half' takes DE, the first half of DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to find it intolerable, which is what not being able to stand it means.

clue.text: US soldiers upheld Constitution — that's distinctive

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a person's constitution is their nature or make-up

explanation.surface: American troops have defended the US Constitution, and that is what sets them apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' turns GIS into SIG, which suits a down entry; 'Constitution' is not the American document but one's make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Used before a noun, as in a chef's signature dish, it means characteristic and individual, i.e. distinctive.

clue.text: Unreliable scoundrel penetrating heart of American

indicators.note: penetrating says one piece goes right into another
heart of keeps only the central letters, dropping two from each end of the word American

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or traitor

explanation.surface: A shifty villain is worming his way into the core of American life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' here means more than one middle letter: it strips two from each end to leave ERIC, which 'penetrating' then opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic behaves irregularly and unpredictably, so it cannot be depended on.

clue.text: Gear of airborne trooper gaining height in flying airplane

indicators.note: gaining says the trooper picks up the following letters after him

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier dropped by air

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters being tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: A paratrooper's kit goes up with him in the aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' reads as describing the plane, but it is the anagram signal; with height added, the shuffle yields PHERNALIA. Note the American spelling 'airplane' is needed for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellaneous equipment and belongings needed for an activity are its gear, the everyday word for such clutter.

clue.text: Fries joints after starter of consommé

indicators.note: after places the joints behind the first letter
a starter comes first, so this takes the opening letter of consommé

parts.note: hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: A meal plan: soup to start, followed by fried potatoes and some roast joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' and 'joints' both look like menu words; one picks C, the other is body joints, HIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Long strips of fried potato are called chips in Britain and fries in America, so the words are equivalent.

clue.text: Not many hurried to see Liberal ousted

indicators.note: ousted means the Liberal is thrown out of the word

parts.note: flew can mean hurried, as in she flew to the door

explanation.surface: Hardly anyone rushed to see the Liberal politician kicked out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousted' removes L from FLEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A small number, hardly any at all, is the meaning of this quantity word.

clue.text: Make redundant, or leave alone

definitions.meaning: to dismiss a worker because the job is no longer needed
to stop bothering or criticising someone, as in 'give it a rest'

explanation.surface: A manager is told to sack someone or simply let them be.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means dismiss staff for lack of work, and also, as a command, stop pestering.

clue.text: Aggressive performer good in a row

indicators.note: in puts the good letter inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as in tiers of seats

explanation.surface: A fierce entertainer, well placed in a line of acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performer' tempts toward the stage, but it means anyone who performs, like a determined competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiercely determined competitor or worker is called a tiger, a big-cat metaphor for ferocity.

clue.text: Method behind story-teller spinning a line

indicators.note: behind puts the method after the reversed storyteller
spinning turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: someone who tells stories, i.e. fibs, is a liar
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A yarn-spinner relies on a technique: spinning a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning a line' looks like a single idiom about telling tales; 'spinning' reverses LIAR to RAIL, and 'line' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway line, such as the West Coast Main Line, is a track and its trains, so the two words overlap.

clue.text: Begin to have a meal, consuming flan

indicators.note: consuming means one piece takes in, or swallows, the other

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper
a tart is a flan, an open pastry dish

explanation.surface: Someone sits down to dinner and tucks into a flan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' belongs naturally to the dinner picture, which hides its job as the container signal; 'to have a meal' is the old verb sup.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means set something going, as when an engine or business is first got under way.

clue.text: Location of non-union members?

parts.note: union here is marriage: people who have never married are said, unkindly, to be left 'on the' ledge where unwanted items sit

explanation.surface: A question about where workers who refuse to join the trade union are sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests trade unions; it means marriage, and the old phrase 'left on the shelf' describes the unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: An unwed person past the usual age is idiomatically said to be 'on the shelf', so the ledge is their place.

clue.text: Struggling near-dunce shows staying-power

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters writhing about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A pupil who is nearly a dunce, battling on, still shows grit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' rearranges the nine letters of NEAR DUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina, the ability to keep going through hardship, is the noun's core sense.

clue.text: Free to continue without observations?

definitions.meaning: not stopped or restrained, as in a disease spreading unhindered
taken literally, having had no checks, that is no inspections or looks over

explanation.surface: Something allowed to carry on with nobody watching it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, literal reading: no checks made.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unrestrained, and also, read literally, not inspected or examined.

clue.text: Equipment beginning to cook chicken here?

definitions.text: Equipment beginning to cook chicken here?

parts.note: kit is equipment

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the first letter of the following word cook

parts.note: a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A question about where you would gather gear to start roasting a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place where poultry is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The room of a house where food is prepared and cooked is where such a bird would be roasted.

clue.text: Billion invested in dull equestrian centre

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, playing on investing money

parts.note: stale means dull or uninteresting

explanation.surface: A billion pounds put into a boring riding establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' sounds financial beside 'Billion' but means put inside: STA-B-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where horses are kept and looked after is a centre for horse-related activity.

clue.text: Pipe, not without content that's free-flowing

parts.note: a flue is a pipe or duct for smoke

indicators.note: without content empties the word not of its middle, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pipe that is not empty lets things flow through it freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without content' takes the inside out of NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or writing that runs smoothly and effortlessly is described as fluent, flowing without hesitation.

clue.text: Incline to adopt right fashion

indicators.note: to adopt means to take in, so the incline word takes the right letter inside

parts.note: to tend is to incline towards something

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined to take up the correct style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incline' and 'fashion' could both be verbs; 'fashion' is the noun, a current style.
explanation.definitionFit: A current style or vogue that many people follow is a trend in fashion.

clue.text: Put off fellow initially probing targets of hunt

indicators.note: probing means going into something, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: deer are the quarry of a traditional hunt

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of fellow

explanation.surface: A hunter is delayed while a companion goes looking for the quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes inside DEER: DE-F-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone, delay till later, is exactly to put something off.

clue.text: A routine in local area network recalled as normal

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the whole thing is read backwards
in puts the routine inside the network

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: An IT manager remembers a routine on the office network as ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: The container gives LARUTAN, then 'recalled' (called back) turns it round; 'routine' as a rut means a dull habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary and expected, in keeping with nature, is natural, synonymous with normal behaviour.

clue.text: Shy sub, half demented

indicators.note: demented means driven out of one's mind, so the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: A timid submarine, half out of its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' seems to cut a word in two, but its letters join SUB as fodder, and 'demented' scrambles all seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easily embarrassed and self-conscious is shyness; it is also the name of one of Snow White's dwarfs.

clue.text: Starts to stagnate in this place

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin settling down and going nowhere in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' is a verb here: to set something down.
explanation.definitionFit: To set or rest something in a position, as in sitting a pot on the stove, means to place it.

clue.text: Part of door fitted into arch, in general

indicators.note: fitted into says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A door component installed in an archway, generally speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from 'arcH IN GEneral'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pivoting metal joint on which a door swings is one of its parts.

clue.text: Consider fellows to have little time for diversion

indicators.note: to have says the fellows take the time letter on after them

parts.note: to entertain an idea is to consider it
men are fellows
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: Think about letting the chaps have a short break for some fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consider' is ENTERTAIN as in entertaining an idea, not hosting guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement or recreation that takes one's mind off things is a diversion.
